keyVerseText: And she conceived again, and bare a son; and said, Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi. Levi: that is, Joined
rootMeaning: The root of לֵוִי (Lêvîy) is derived from the Hebrew verb לָוָה (lâvâh), which conveys the idea of joining, attaching, or cleaving to something. This root emphasizes a close, inseparable connection, often implying accompaniment or union. Beyond the simple English name 'Levi,' the root meaning enriches our understanding by highlighting a relational bond—being 'joined to' or 'attached'—which reflects the underlying significance of the name in its original context.
usageInScripture: The word לֵוִי appears 64 times in Scripture, predominantly translated as 'of Levi' (52 occurrences), indicating its frequent use as a tribal or familial designation. Other translations such as 'and Levi' and simply 'Levi' occur less often but consistently point to the same individual or tribe. This consistency in translation underscores the importance of Levi as both a person—the third son of Jacob—and the progenitor of the Levites, a tribe intimately connected to religious duties and service. The usage reveals a strong identity link to the concept of being 'joined' or 'attached' within Israel's covenant community.
theologicalSignificance: The original meaning of לֵוִי as 'joined to' carries profound theological weight in understanding God's covenant people. Levi, as the ancestor of the Levites, symbolizes a people set apart and intimately connected to the service of God, especially in attending to the priestly duties alongside Aaron. This notion of attachment or joining reflects the believer's call to be united with God and His purposes. It also prefigures the New Testament theme of believers being joined to Christ, the ultimate High Priest, emphasizing a spiritual union that defines identity and service. Recognizing Levi's name as 'joined' enriches our appreciation of God's design for community, worship, and holiness.
keyVerseReflection: Genesis 29:34 states, 'Now this time will my husband be joined unto me, because I have born him three sons: therefore was his name called Levi.' Here, the name Levi explicitly means 'Joined,' directly connecting the personal name to the relational hope expressed by Leah. This verse reveals that the name is not merely an identifier but a declaration of intimate union and faithfulness within family relationships. The word לֵוִי thus embodies both a personal and communal reality of being joined, which resonates throughout Scripture as a foundational theme of covenant relationship.
